title: fix(profile): show skeleton for username/avatar during profile load
body:
## Summary

- Wraps the username text and the colored-identicon avatar on the profile header in a `Skeletonizer` with a 7-second `_timeoutExpired` fallthrough, mirroring the existing `_ProfileStatsRow` pattern at `profile_header_widget.dart:680-770`.
- Before: on cold-start (or any rebuild before the user's Kind 0 resolves), the header rendered a deterministic but real-looking *Adjective Animal Number* name (e.g. *"Shawn Shine 47"*) plus a colored identicon. New users misread the brief flash as their identity being silently changed (see #4054 — *"username briefly changed to shawnshine"*).
- After: the username/avatar shimmer until either the profile loads or the 7-second timeout expires. After the timeout the existing generated-name / identicon fallback kicks in, preserving the steady-state path for users who genuinely have no Kind 0 published (per @hm21's triage on #4054).

### Wiring details

- New `bool isLoading` on `UserName.fromPubKey` and `UserName.fromUserProfile`. When true, the widget early-returns a `Skeletonizer` over a fixed-width l10n placeholder string (`userNameSkeletonPlaceholder`) rather than resolving the AsyncValue or falling back to a generated name. The existing un-gated AsyncValue arm is unchanged so all ~11 other callers keep today's behaviour.
- New `bool isLoading` on `UserAvatar`. When true, the rendered avatar is wrapped in `Skeletonizer(effect: vineSkeletonEffect, …)` instead of painting the deterministic `_Placeholder` identicon.
- `_ProfileAvatarWithColor` and `_ProfileNameAndBio` converted to `StatefulWidget`s that own a 7-second `_timeoutExpired` `Timer` identical in shape to `_ProfileStatsRowState`.
- `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState.build` now derives a single `isLoadingIdentity` boolean from `MyProfileBloc` state (own profile) or `fetchUserProfileProvider` AsyncValue (other profile) and threads it to both children. Cached profiles short-circuit to `isLoading: false` so warm-starts never flash a skeleton.

### Steady-state behaviour preserved

- `MyProfileLoading(profile: cached)` → `isLoadingIdentity = false` (we have data to show; do not skeleton).
- `MyProfileError(notFound)` → `isLoadingIdentity = false` (the generated-name fallback is the *truthful* state for users with no Kind 0).
- After 7-second timeout → children flip back to `isLoading: false` even if the parent still says loading, so a stuck relay does not produce an infinite shimmer.

Closes #4163.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter gen-l10n` regenerated all 16 generated locale files; staged.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/user_name_skeleton_test.dart test/widgets/user_avatar_skeleton_test.dart` — 7 / 7 pass.
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/` — 80 pass (including 7 new "Identity skeleton (#4163)" cases plus the timeout-fallthrough test under fake clock advancement).
- [x] Wider sweep: `flutter test test/widgets/profile/ test/widgets/user_name_*.dart test/widgets/user_avatar_*.dart test/widgets/comprehensive_user_avatar_test.dart` — 215 pass, 4 pre-existing golden skips.
- [ ] Manual: sign out, sign back in (or fresh-install). Expect: header avatar and username show a brief shimmer, then transition to the real identity. **Crucially**, no *Adjective Animal Number* string flashes on the user's own profile during the loading window.
- [ ] Manual: open another user's profile that's not in cache. Expect same shimmer behaviour, then real identity.
- [ ] Manual: simulate a stuck relay (airplane mode) on a brand-new account. After ~7 s the skeleton dissolves and the existing *Adjective Animal Number* fallback appears (steady-state path preserved for users who genuinely have no Kind 0).
- [ ] Translations: 16 non-English locales now report 1 additional untranslated message (`userNameSkeletonPlaceholder`) — strings team to land translations separately, the placeholder text is hidden behind the shimmer so visual impact is zero.

## Related

- Sibling PR #4182 (closes #4164 — videos-tab loading state) ships separately, no file overlap.

title: fix(profile): keep loading state until profile videos fetch completes
body:
## Summary

Profile pages can show a premature `No videos` empty state before the profile video fetch has actually completed.

This came out of the investigation on #4054. The current behavior makes it look like a user has no videos when we are still in a loading phase.

## Expected

The profile should remain in a loading state until the relevant profile video loading steps are complete.

## Actual

`No videos` can render too early, then later flip to showing the user's videos.

## Why this needs its own issue

This is a concrete, actionable bug with a plausible fix, unlike the other mixed symptoms in #4054 that still need logs or a reliable repro.

## Context

- Source issue: #4054
- Related triage comment: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4054#issuecomment-4408728296

title: fix(perf): profile videos tab feels laggy for ~1s when opening profile with 50+ videos

labels.name: performance
labels.description: App startup, video playback, rendering, and memory

body:
## Summary

Opening another user's profile with 50+ videos shows a ~1s freeze right after the loading spinner clears, before the grid becomes interactive. Surfaced in [PR #4182 review](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4182#pullrequestreview-4257513564) by @hm21.

> *"does it also feel super laggy for you when opening the profile of someone who has 50+ videos when everything is loaded for maybe 1s? It's definitely not caused by this PR, so if you notice it too, it's probably something we should tackle in a separate PR."*

## Repro

1. Cold-launch the app, sign in.
2. Navigate to a profile with **50+ videos** (the `subscribeToUserVideos` limit is 50, so this is the boundary case where all events arrive in a single relay EOSE burst).
3. Observe: the loading spinner clears, then the screen freezes for ~1s before the videos grid responds to scroll/tap.

## Root cause analysis

Three contributing layers; only #1 affects the *other-user* repro the reviewer flagged:

1. **Image-decode + `ImageCache` thrash on first paint of 50 thumbnails** *(primary, affects all profile types)*
   - `mobile/lib/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail.dart:32` wraps `VineCachedImage` **without a `memCacheWidth`** constraint.
   - Without it, `cached_network_image` decodes thumbnails at native CDN resolution (typically 720×1280 ≈ 3 MB each). 50 tiles × ~3 MB ≈ 150 MB, which exceeds Flutter's default `ImageCache` budget (100 MB / 100 entries) → cache thrashing, repeated decodes, and a heavy GPU-upload spike on first paint.
   - Precedent in-repo: `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/video_notification_row.dart:164` already uses `memCacheWidth: 200` for 56dp tiles.

2. **`ProfileVideosGrid.build()` rebuild churn on `BackgroundPublishBloc` progress ticks** *(own-profile only)*
   - Already tracked in #3605 (item #1).

3. **De-dup + `DateTime.now()` parsing + side-effecting `downloadFile()` inside `build()`** *(own-profile only)*
   - Already tracked in #3603.

For the reviewer's specific repro (opening *someone else's* profile), `isOwnProfile=false` makes #2 and #3 no-ops. The 1s lag is dominated by #1, plus the relay-burst provider work in `_relayVideosSnapshot` → `authorVideos` (re-sorts the entire bucket on every call, `mobile/lib/services/video_event_service.dart:886`) → `filterVideoList` (two O(N) passes, `video_event_service.dart:633-697`).

## Proposed fix (scoped to this issue)

Add `memCacheWidth` to `ProfileTabThumbnail`'s `VineCachedImage`. Single-file change benefits **every** profile tab grid that shares the widget (videos / liked / reposts / saved / collabs / comments).

The deeper provider-cascade work (`authorVideos` re-sort, double-pass `filterVideoList`, multiple state-emit re-renders during cold-load) is out of scope for this fix and should be triaged separately if QA still observes residual jank after the decode fix.

## Related work (not duplicated here)

- #3603 — Move profile grid de-duplication out of `build()` (open, assigned).
- #3605 — `context.watch` causing unnecessary widget rebuilds (open, calls out `profile_videos_grid.dart`).

title: fix(profile): preserve arbitrary Kind 0 fields across profile edits
body:
## Summary

Closes #4175.

Editing a profile silently dropped any Kind 0 field the typed `UserProfile` model didn't know about — `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, `bot`, NIP-39 `i` tags, custom client keys, future NIP additions. PR #4022 patched the symptom for `nip05` only; this PR generalizes the fix to every field.

## What changes

### Two-layer fix

1. **`ProfileRepository.saveProfileEvent` now seeds from the freshest relay Kind 0** before composing the new event content. Relay events round-trip through `UserProfile.fromNostrEvent`, which preserves the full content as `rawData` — so unknown fields survive byte-identical. Falls back to `currentProfile` on relay timeout/failure.
2. **`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` now mirrors the typed REST fields into `rawData`** (defense-in-depth — kicks in when the relay fetch fails). The Funnelcake REST API does not expose the raw Kind 0 JSON, so unknown fields can only be recovered via the relay seed.

### Merge contract

The new `saveProfileEvent` builds the published content from a copy of `seed.rawData`, then applies a small set of explicit deltas:

- **Editable fields** (`display_name`, `about`, `picture`, `banner`): caller's value wins. Empty/null **removes the key** — the form is pre-populated from the seed, so an empty submit is treated as an explicit clear.
- **`nip05`**: keeps the race-protected clear semantics from #4022 — only removed when `clearNip05: true`.
- **Every other key**: passes through from the seed untouched.

Also drops the previous behavior of writing explicit `null` for unset editable fields; those keys are now omitted entirely. Semantically equivalent on all major Nostr clients, and consistent with how unknown-field preservation works (no key === unset).

## Why this matters

A divine-mobile user who edits their bio in our app no longer silently rewrites their Kind 0 in a way that erases work done in any other client (Damus, Amethyst, Primal, etc.). Lightning zaps via `lud16` keep working. NIP-39 identity proofs survive. Future NIPs that we don't yet model survive automatically.

## Tests

The load-bearing invariant is pinned by a new test in `profile_repository_test.dart`:

> "preserves arbitrary unknown fields when seeded from a relay-fetched Kind 0"

The seed has `bot`, `i`, `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, and a `weird_future_field`. Editing only `display_name` produces a published event whose every non-`display_name` key is byte-identical to the seed.

Other new tests:
- `falls back to currentProfile when relay seed fetch fails`
- `mirrors typed REST fields into rawData` (`user_profile_test.dart`)
- `omits null typed fields from rawData` (`user_profile_test.dart`)

Existing `saveProfileEvent` tests were updated for the new omit-empty-keys contract. The #4022 nip05 preservation regression test was kept intact.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test` in `mobile/packages/models` — 103 passing
- [x] `flutter test` in `mobile/packages/profile_repository` — 195 passing
- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/blocs/profile_editor/` — 71 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — clean
- [ ] Manual: log in as a user with `lud16` set in another client; edit display_name in divine-mobile; inspect published Kind 0 via `wss://relay.divine.video` — confirm `lud16` is present.

## Out of scope

- Funnelcake REST returning the raw Kind 0 event JSON — would let the typed REST factory carry unknown fields too. Track in `divine-funnelcake`. Until then, the relay seed step is the only path that preserves unknown fields.
- Same `rawData`-loss pattern on other replaceable kinds (kind 3 follow lists, kind 10002 relay lists, kind 10000 mute lists). Worth a survey but not in this PR.

title: feat(popular): add time-period filter to Explore → Popular tab
body:
Closes #4148

## Description

Adds a 5-chip time-period filter to the Explore → Popular tab, deep-linkable via `?period=…` query param.

**The chips:** Right Now · Today · This Week · This Month · All Time

- **Right Now** keeps the current behavior — `/api/videos?sort=watching` (24h CDN view count, no age decay).
- **Today / This Week / This Month / All Time** route through funnelcake's `/api/leaderboard/videos?period=…` endpoint (newly wired into the funnelcake client).

**Architecture** (per `.claude/rules/architecture.md`):
- UI chip taps push URL changes (`context.go('/explore/tab/popular?period=<slug>')`)
- `ExploreScreen.didChangeDependencies` syncs `?period=` from `GoRouterState` into a Riverpod `StateProvider<LeaderboardPeriod?>` (post-frame to avoid build-phase writes)
- `popularVideosFeedProvider` watches the StateProvider; period flip triggers a fresh `_loadFirstPage`
- `VideosRepository.getPopularVideos({period: ...})` dispatches to `/api/leaderboard/videos` when period is set, falls through to existing watching/NIP-50 path when null
- A sealed `_PopularCursor` (timestamp vs offset) keeps pagination semantics straight across the two paths

**URL format:**
- `/explore/tab/popular` — Right Now (default)
- `/explore/tab/popular?period=today|week|month|alltime` — windowed leaderboard

`fromUrlSlug` accepts both `today` and `day` for back-compat; the canonical emit is always `today` for shareability.

**l10n:** 6 new keys (label + 5 chip names) added to `app_en.arb` only; allowlisted in `_knownUntranslatedDebt` in `arb_consistency_test.dart`. Translations land in a follow-up locale-pass PR.

## What's NOT in this PR

A **New / Classics** content axis on the Popular tab is intentionally **out of scope**. The combination `Classics × {Today,Week,Month,All Time}` is server-blocked: `/api/leaderboard/videos` silently ignores unknown query params (verified by live probe — `?platform=vine` returns identical bytes to the bare query) and the response items don't include a `platform` field at all, so client-side filtering also isn't possible.

The funnelcake-side ask is to:
1. Add `platform=` query support to `/api/leaderboard/videos` (matching `/api/videos`)
2. Include `platform` in the leaderboard response items

Once that ships, the kind axis can land as a small follow-up PR (one `popularKindProvider`, one chip row, no new endpoint plumbing).

`Right Now × Classics` works today via the existing `?sort=watching&platform=vine` combo and could ship in this PR — but it'd be a half-feature ("kind axis only available on Right Now") with confusing UX, so we're holding the entire kind axis until the server work lands.

## Test plan

Automated:
- Funnelcake client: 10 new tests covering URL construction, all 4 period wire values, offset pagination, response edge cases, error paths
- Repository: 5 new tests covering period dispatch, offset propagation, no-NIP-50-fallback semantics, period-keyed cache, watching-path regression
- Provider: 3 new tests covering period propagation, default null behavior, rebuild-on-flip
- Widget (`PopularFilterBar`): 6 tests covering chip rendering, selected state, URL push, urlSlug-vs-wireValue distinction, Right Now clears `?period=`
- Widget (`PopularVideosTab`): 1 smoke test that the filter bar renders above the grid
- Screen (URL → provider sync): 5 tests covering ?period=week, today-slug back-compat, bare URL clears, invalid value, no-GoRouter no-op
- l10n consistency: existing test extended with the 6 new keys
- **Full mobile suite**: 8344 pass / 400 skip / 0 fail post-rebase

Manual (still needed before merge):
- [ ] Tap each chip on a real device, verify URL updates and grid refreshes
- [ ] Deep-link `/explore/tab/popular?period=week` from cold start, verify correct chip is selected and grid loads
- [ ] Background the app for 10s, return — verify selected chip survives
- [ ] Verify scroll-to-hide animation works for the new chip row alongside the existing trending hashtags row
- [ ] Pull-to-refresh on each window — confirm correct endpoint is hit (network logs)
- [ ] Test with `flutter run` in different system text scales — chip row should grow with text, not clip

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Notes

- Implementation plan is committed at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-08-popular-tab-time-period-filter.md` for future maintainers.
- The popular feed provider keeps its private cursor field (refactored to a sealed `_PopularCursor`) — extending the existing legacy Riverpod pattern rather than introducing a BLoC migration. Future cleanup item.
- Cache key changed from `'popular'` to `'popular:<wireValue>'` for windowed periods; the Right Now path keeps the bare `'popular'` key for backward compatibility.
- 4 fix commits included: cursor/period race guard, accessibility-safe ConstrainedBox, layout-safety in unbounded parents, GoRouter-absence no-op. Each addresses an issue caught by automated review during plan execution.

When editing videos with multiple clips and wanting specific moments to play slower or faster.

title: feat(video): show likers/reposters list when owner taps like/repost
body:
Closes #4173

## Summary
- Tapping Like or Repost on your own video used to toggle your own like/repost — meaningless on a video you authored. It now opens a full-screen list of the users who liked or reposted that video instead.
- Adds a new repository method on each engagement-tracking package (`likes_repository.fetchEventLikers`, `reposts_repository.fetchEventReposters`) that pulls reactor / reposter pubkeys directly from relays. Funnelcake's REST API only exposes aggregate engagement counts, so the lists have to come from a kind 7 / kind 6+16 relay query, deduped across `e` / `a` tags and with kind 5 deletions filtered out.
- New `VideoEngagementBloc` + `VideoEngagementListScreen` (Page/View) at `/video/:eventId/likers` and `/video/:eventId/reposters`, with an optional `?a=` query param for addressable Kind 30000+ events. The list reuses the existing `UserProfileTile` (without the follow CTA) for rendering.
- Threads `isOwnVideo` from the existing check in `VideoOverlayActionColumn` down into `LikeActionButton` and `RepostActionButton`. On the owner's own video, the tap navigates instead of dispatching the toggle event.

## Known limitations / follow-ups
- The lists are loaded once when the screen opens (single relay query, returns when EOSE fires). They don't subscribe for live updates of new likes / reposts that arrive while the screen is open. Pull-to-refresh re-runs the query. Eventually we'll want a live-subscription-backed list and pagination once it matters; this v1 ships the full list because most own-video engagement counts are small.
- Five new ARB keys (`videoEngagementLikersTitle` / `RepostersTitle` / `LikersEmpty` / `RepostersEmpty` / `LoadFailed`) are added in English and allowlisted in `arb_consistency_test.dart` so non-English locales fall back to English until the next translation pass — same pattern as the recent Edit / Report button additions.

## Test plan
- [ ] As the video author, tap the Like button on your own video → likers list opens; back returns to the feed; refresh re-queries.
- [ ] As the video author, tap the Repost button on your own video → reposters list opens; tapping a profile pushes their profile screen.
- [ ] As another user, tap Like on someone else's video → still toggles like (count flips, heart fills).
- [ ] As another user, tap Repost on someone else's video → still toggles repost.
- [ ] Empty-state copy renders when no one has liked / reposted yet.
- [ ] Failure state renders + retry works when the relay query fails.
- [ ] Both addressable (Kind 34236 with d-tag) and non-addressable target events work — the addressable id is forwarded as `?a=` and merged with the `e`-tag results.

title: feat(invites): retry transient consume failures with session preservation
body:
Closes #4069

## Summary

PR 2 of 3 for #3795 (Liz's prescribed sequence: telemetry → retry → classification tightening).

- Adds `isRetryable()` and `retryConsume()` helpers to `InviteErrorUtils` -- classifies `temporary` and `authFailure` errors as retryable, retries up to 3x with 2s delay
- Replaces the narrow 409-only retry loop in `EmailVerificationCubit` with the broader `retryConsume()` wrapper
- Wraps both `DivineAuthCubit` consume paths (session-based sign-in and anonymous skip) with `retryConsume()`
- Persists `KeycastSession` via `session.save()` before consume in both session-based paths, so the session survives exhausted retries
- Each retry generates a fresh NIP-98 timestamp (via `_createAuthorizationHeader` using `DateTime.now()`), addressing clock-skew failures

**Stacked on #4065 (PR 1: telemetry).** This prescribed sequence is designed to land incrementally -- PR 1 adds observability, PR 2 adds retry, PR 3 tightens classification based on production data. Stacking lets each PR land and ship in order. Retarget to `main` after PR 1 merges.

## Retryable vs terminal

| Classification | Examples | Retried? |
|---|---|---|
| `temporary` | timeout, network, 5xx, 429, storage_error | Yes |
| `authFailure` | clock skew, auth_invalid, client_auth_failed | Yes |
| `alreadyUsed` | invite_already_used, user_already_joined | No |
| `invalid` | not_found, revoked, expired | No |
| `creatorFull` | creator_page_full | No |
| `unknown` | unclassified errors | No |

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `mobile/lib/utils/invite_error_utils.dart` | Add `isRetryable()` + `retryConsume()` |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart` | Replace 409 loop, add `session.save()` |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/divine_auth/divine_auth_cubit.dart` | Wrap both consume paths, add `session.save()` |

## Test plan

- [x] `isRetryable()` tested for all 6 failure reasons (48 tests in invite_error_utils_test)
- [x] `retryConsume()` tested: first success, retry+succeed, terminal rethrow, exhausted rethrow, log verification, maxAttempts
- [x] EmailVerificationCubit: transient retry succeeds, exhausted retry fails, terminal error not retried
- [x] DivineAuthCubit: session-based retry on transient error, anonymous path retry on transient error
- [x] All 140 tests pass across 3 test suites
- [x] `flutter analyze` clean (only pre-existing notification_repository infos)
- [ ] Verify retry is invisible to user (no UI changes)
- [ ] Verify session recovery after app kill during retry window

## Spec

Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-invite-consume-retry-design.md`

title: feat(profile): verified-account chips + in-app verifier (closes #3933)
body:
## Summary
- Adds the `verifier_client` package wrapping `https://verifier.divine.video` (HTTP client + models + exceptions).
- Preserves raw event tags on `UserProfile` so `IdentityClaimsRepository` can parse NIP-39 `i` tags into `IdentityClaim` records and verify them via the verifier batch API.
- Wires the repository into `MyProfileBloc` and `OtherProfileBloc` so each `*Loaded`/`*Updated` state carries `verifiedClaims`; renders a `VerifiedAccountsRow` of tap-to-launch chips on the view-profile header and the edit-profile screen.
- Adds a new `VerifierWebViewScreen` hosting verifier.divine.video in an in-app WebView. No postMessage bridge — the verifier publishes its own kind 0 update via the user's existing signer flow.
- `ProfileEditorBloc` exposes `VerifierStatus` with `VerifierLaunchRequested` / `VerifierWebViewDismissed` events. UI-level `BlocListener` pushes the WebView and, after dismiss, dispatches `MyProfileFetchRequested` so newly-verified chips appear immediately.
- Replaces the old hand-rolled "Username + Proof URL" flow with a single "Get verified" CTA tile that hands off to the verifier service.

Builds on the npub-demotion work that landed in #3941. Closes #3933.

This was originally split into a stack (#3954 + #3955); collapsed back into a single PR for easier review.

## Test Plan
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` clean
- [x] Pre-push test sweep green (~547 tests)
- [x] Package tests green: `verifier_client`, `profile_repository`, `models`
- [x] Bloc tests green: `my_profile_bloc`, `other_profile_bloc`, `profile_editor_bloc`
- [x] Screen / widget tests green: `profile_setup_screen`, `profile_header_widget`, `verified_account_chip`, `verified_accounts_row`, `verifier_webview_screen`
- [ ] Manual: open own profile with NIP-39 `i` tags → chips render after verifier responds; tapping a chip opens the platform profile in the system browser
- [ ] Manual: open another user's profile → same behaviour
- [ ] Manual: open Edit Profile → "Verified accounts" header + "Get verified" tile present (no manual proof-URL form)
- [ ] Manual: tap "Get verified" → WebView opens at verifier.divine.video
- [ ] Manual: complete a verification (e.g. GitHub) → press back → newly verified chip appears under the bio after kind 0 refresh

title: fix(reports): use environment relay for content reports
body:
## Summary

- Content reports (Kind 1984) were hardcoded to `wss://relay.divine.video`, ignoring the app's environment configuration
- Reports now target the relay from `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`, so staging/test builds send reports to the correct environment relay
- `ContentReportingService` accepts `moderationRelayUrl` as a constructor parameter instead of using a static constant
- The reporting provider remains auto-dispose and now watches `currentEnvironmentProvider`, so it stays aligned with runtime environment changes without caching a stale relay URL or stale initialization state

## Known limitation

This fix routes reports to the environment's default relay, which solves the single-relay staging/test case. When connected to multiple relays, reports still go to the environment default rather than the relay the reported content was fetched from. A full fix would thread `Event.sources` from the nostr SDK through `VideoEvent` into `reportContent()`. See #4019 for details.

## Test plan

- [x] Staging build sends Kind 1984 reports to `wss://relay.staging.dvines.org`
- [x] Production build continues to send reports to `wss://relay.divine.video`
- [x] `flutter test --no-pub test/services/content_reporting_service_test.dart`

Closes #3997

## Summary

- **Moves** the custom NIP-05 control out of Edit Profile and into a new dedicated screen at **Settings → Nostr → Account → "NIP-05 address"**.
- Available by default — no feature flag, no settings gate. Discoverable from the Settings hub.

## Why

The original placement on Edit Profile was both hard to find (users couldn't find where to set NIP-05 at all) and easy to misconfigure (a single tap of a checkbox under the username field flipped them off divine.video onto a domain they likely didn't control). - **Removed** `ExternalNip05Section` and the external NIP-05 controller / focus node from `profile_setup_screen.dart`. The save path still preserves the existing external NIP-05 from editor state.
- **Removed** `advanced_identity_options_provider` (and the gate built around it).
- **l10n**: removed `nostrSettingsAdvancedIdentityOptions*`; added `nostrSettingsNip05Address`, `nostrSettingsNip05AddressSubtitle`, `nostrSettingsNip05SaveAction`, `nostrSettingsNip05Saved`, `nostrSettingsNip05SaveFailed`. Confirm dialog keys (`profileSetupNip05Confirm*`) kept and reused. Propagated to all 16 non-English locales.

title: fix(notifications): clear unread badge by syncing Riverpod cache on inbox open
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #4144 (notification badge count not clearing) — duplicate of #4048
- Supersedes #4149 (close that PR after this lands)
- Two-bug fix: an `_onStarted` / `_onMarkAllRead` ordering race in the BLoC, plus a BLoC ↔ Riverpod cache desync that left the bottom-nav badge stale until the 5-min auto-refresh

## Why

The notifications subsystem is mid-migration to BLoC, but the bottom-nav badge and inbox segmented-toggle count are still driven by the legacy `relayNotificationsProvider` (Riverpod) cache. Opening the inbox marks-read in the BLoC's `NotificationRepository` — both stacks POST to the same server endpoint, but neither propagates to the other's in-memory cache, so the badge stays unread until Riverpod's 5-min auto-refresh fires. Users perceive this as "notifications not going away."

The pre-existing PR #4149 attempted a tactical bridge by calling `relayNotificationsProvider.notifier.markAllAsRead()` from `NotificationsView.initState`. The reviewer (@NotThatKindOfDrLiz) blocked it on three points: a duplicated weaker `_onStarted` mark-read that bypassed the rollback path #4034 added, fan-out across the five `NotificationsView` tabs mounted by `TabBarView`, and missing test coverage of the side effect. This PR addresses all three.

## What changed

**`mobile/lib/notifications/bloc/notification_feed_bloc.dart`**
- `_onStarted` re-dispatches `NotificationFeedMarkAllRead` after the loaded state is emitted, instead of inlining a weaker mark-read. The existing `_onMarkAllRead` rollback / `addError` path runs uniformly.

**`mobile/lib/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page.dart`** and **`notifications_page.dart`**
- Both pages now own a single Riverpod sync via `ref.listenManual` with `fireImmediately: true`, guarded by a `_relaySynced` one-shot flag plus an unread-check on the resolved provider state. Fires exactly once per page open whether the provider is warm (already loaded by the bottom nav) or cold-starting.
- Standalone `NotificationsPage` is converted from `ConsumerWidget` to `ConsumerStatefulWidget`. `_InboxNotificationsScaffold` is converted from `StatefulWidget` to `ConsumerStatefulWidget`.

**`mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_view.dart`**
- Adds a `mounted` guard inside the post-frame callback. Note: the per-`NotificationsView` Riverpod call from PR #4149's diff is intentionally absent here — the side effect lives at the page level so it doesn't fan out across the five `TabBarView` children.

## Tests

- BLoC tests: assert `_notificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` is called once after `NotificationFeedStarted` with unread items, and `verifyNever` when the loaded page is already all-read. Existing `isFollowingBack` derivation test updated for the additional optimistic-mark-read state. Default `markAllAsRead` stub added to the parent `setUp` so existing `NotificationFeedStarted` tests don't regress.
- New `mobile/test/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page_test.dart`: verifies the Riverpod side effect fires exactly once per inbox open, not at all when nothing is unread, and stays at one call after swiping through all five filter tabs.
- Extended `notifications_page_test.dart` with parallel assertions for the standalone `/notifications/:index` route.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications/ test/screens/inbox/` — 252 passing
- [ ] Manual: launch app, trigger a notification (follow yourself from a second account), confirm bottom-nav badge appears, open Inbox → Notifications, return to Home, confirm badge clears immediately
- [ ] Manual: repeat against the standalone `/notifications/0` route via the tab-history back-navigation path in `app_shell.dart`
- [ ] CI: build / Analyze / Tests / Format / Generated Files

## Out of scope (followup)

The dual-stack architecture itself remains. The proper destination — promote `NotificationRepository.watchUnreadCount()` to a stream and add a `NotificationBadgeCubit` mirroring `DmUnreadCountCubit` — is captured in `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-09-issue4144-notification-badge-desync-brainstorm.md` as Approach C. Tracked separately in #3596 (Delete dual notification system) so this hotfix stays small.

title: Profile edits silently drop lud16, lud06, website, and other Kind 0 fields when loaded from REST API
body:
## Summary

Editing a profile silently strips every field beyond the explicit form inputs (`display_name`, `about`, `nip05`, `picture`, `banner`) when the loaded `currentProfile` came from the Funnelcake REST API. Most notably this means **lightning addresses (`lud16`, `lud06`)** and **`website`** disappear from the user's published Kind 0 the next time they edit any profile field.

This is the **same root cause** that #4021 / #4022 fixed for `nip05` specifically, generalized to every other field. The earlier fix added a one-off fallback for nip05 only, so today nip05 is preserved but lud16/lud06/website/bot/etc. are not.

## Root cause

`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` in `mobile/packages/models/lib/src/user_profile.dart:99` populates the typed fields from the REST response but sets `rawData: const {}`:

```dart
factory UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound(UserProfileFound result, {String? eventIdPrefix}) {
  final p = result.profile;
  return UserProfile(
    pubkey: p.pubkey,
    name: p.name,
    displayName: p.displayName,
    about: p.about,
    picture: p.picture,
    banner: p.banner,
    website: p.website,        // ← stored in typed field
    nip05: p.nip05,            // ← stored in typed field
    lud16: p.lud16,            // ← stored in typed field
    rawData: const {},         // ← but rawData is empty
    createdAt: DateTime.now(),
    eventId: '${eventIdPrefix ?? 'rest'}-${p.pubkey}',
  );
}
```

`ProfileRepository.saveProfileEvent` (`mobile/packages/profile_repository/lib/src/profile_repository.dart:529`) then composes the Kind 0 content by spreading `currentProfile.rawData` first:

```dart
final profileContent = {
  if (currentProfile != null) ...currentProfile.rawData,    // empty for REST profiles
  'display_name': displayName,
  'about': about,
  'nip05': ?effectiveNip05,    // special-cased fallback to currentProfile.nip05 (lines 523-527)
  'picture': picture,
  'banner': banner,
};
```

Result: a profile loaded from the REST API loses everything that isn't explicitly in this dict on the next save. The nip05 special-case from #4022 is the only field that survives — `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, `bot`, `nip05_verified`, and any custom-client fields are dropped.

## Reproduction

1. User has a Kind 0 with `lud16`, `nip05`, `website`, `display_name`, `about`, `picture`, `banner` (e.g. published from another client like Damus, Amethyst, Primal).
2. User opens divine-mobile. The profile loads via the Funnelcake REST API path (`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound`) — `rawData` is empty.
3. User taps Edit Profile, changes their bio or avatar, taps Save.
4. App publishes a Kind 0 containing only `{display_name, about, nip05, picture, banner}`. **`lud16` is gone.** **`website` is gone.** Any other custom field is gone.
5. Lightning zaps to this user's profile now fail; their website link disappears in other clients; etc.

This is a Nostr cross-client compatibility break — a divine.video user editing their bio in our app silently rewrites their public profile in a way that erases work done in any other client.

## Why the prior fix is not enough

#4022 added a targeted fallback inside `saveProfileEvent`:

```dart
final existingNip05 = (currentProfile?.rawData.containsKey('nip05') ?? false)
    ? null
    : currentProfile?.nip05;
final effectiveNip05 = resolvedNip05 ?? existingNip05;
```

That works for nip05 because `nip05` is one of the typed fields hoisted out of the raw event. But every *other* field that lives in Kind 0 needs the same treatment, and adding case-by-case fallbacks isn't sustainable — Kind 0 is an open dictionary by spec.

## Proposed fix

Pick one (in order of preference):

### Option A — REST returns the raw Kind 0 (best, requires funnelcake)

`/api/users/{pubkey}` and the bulk profile endpoints should include the raw Kind 0 event JSON (or at minimum the parsed `content` object) in the response. `UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` then populates `rawData` from that. This restores the round-trip invariant that `currentProfile.rawData` contains every field the user has ever set.

Cross-repo coordination needed with divine-funnelcake — this is the right long-term fix.

### Option B — Fetch the live Kind 0 from a relay before publishing (mobile-only)

Before `saveProfileEvent` constructs the new content, query relays for the user's most recent Kind 0 and parse its content as the seed for `profileContent`, ignoring `currentProfile.rawData` entirely when it's empty. Slower (adds a round-trip on every Save) but doesn't require any funnelcake change and is robust against any REST-source mapping that drops fields.

### Option C — Mirror typed fields into rawData on REST construction (workaround)

In `UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound`, build `rawData` from the typed fields:

```dart
rawData: {
  if (p.name != null) 'name': p.name,
  if (p.displayName != null) 'display_name': p.displayName,
  if (p.about != null) 'about': p.about,
  if (p.picture != null) 'picture': p.picture,
  if (p.banner != null) 'banner': p.banner,
  if (p.website != null) 'website': p.website,
  if (p.nip05 != null) 'nip05': p.nip05,
  if (p.lud16 != null) 'lud16': p.lud16,
  if (p.lud06 != null) 'lud06': p.lud06,
},
```

Cheap, no network round-trip, fixes every field the typed layer already knows about — but **does not preserve fields the typed layer doesn't know about** (e.g. custom client fields, `bot`, future NIP additions). Should be an interim mitigation, not the final fix.

I'd recommend shipping Option C immediately as a stop-gap and tracking Option A or B as the durable solution.

## Impact

- Any divine-mobile user whose initial profile load goes through the REST API (which is the *primary* path now per the project's "always prefer funnelcake REST" guidance) and who edits their profile in our app.
- Loses lightning zaps until they re-add their lud16 in another client.
- Loses their website link, custom client fields, NIP-39 external identity proofs (if stored in Kind 0), etc.
- Cross-client experience: divine-mobile is a destructive editor for Kind 0 from the perspective of other Nostr clients.

## Related

- #4021 / #4022 — fix for nip05-specific symptom of this bug (merged 2026-05-06). The PR description and this issue's root-cause analysis are the same; #4022 just fixed one field.
- #2285 / #2294 — `UserProfile.fromFunnelcake()` factory introduced the empty `rawData: const {}`.

## Verification (for reviewer)

Reproduce by:
1. `git grep -n "rawData: const {}" mobile/packages/models/lib/src/user_profile.dart`
2. `git grep -n "...currentProfile.rawData" mobile/packages/profile_repository/`
3. Confirm via test: load profile via REST, edit display name only, assert published Kind 0 retains `lud16` from the prior event. (No such test exists today — the PR for the fix should add one.)

title: fix(security): strip BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth wire (#3359)
body:
## Description

Phase 1 emergency block for #3359 — strips the user's nsec from the
Keycast OAuth registration wire on both channels:

- `body['nsec']` field in `POST /api/headless/register`
- `<random>.<nsec1...>` suffix embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier`
  (later POSTed as `code_verifier` to `/api/oauth/token`)

The fix removes the parameters from the `keycast_flutter` package API
entirely so a future caller cannot re-introduce the leak. A POSIX-grep
CI guard locks the rule in.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3359

**Cross-repo coordination:** divinevideo/keycast#197 tracks the
server-side proof-of-possession redesign that Phase 2 depends on.
This PR ships **without** preserving BYOK identity binding — that is
restored once Phase 2 lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ❌ Breaking change (the public `KeycastOAuth.headlessRegister` and `KeycastOAuth.getAuthorizationUrl` APIs no longer accept `nsec` — intentional, for security)

## Trade-off

Until Phase 2 ships, BYOK secure-account upgrades fall through to the
server's auto-generate path. The user's existing local pubkey identity
is **not preserved** across the upgrade, but the local nsec stays
on-device and never crosses the network. This is the intentional
emergency-block trade-off — stop the leak today, restore identity
preservation in Phase 2 (depends on divinevideo/keycast#197).

## What's in this PR

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart` | `generateVerifier` no longer takes `nsec`; verifier is always pure-random base64url |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart` | `getAuthorizationUrl` & `headlessRegister` drop `nsec`/`byokPubkey` parameters; `body['nsec']` removed; `byok_pubkey` URL param removed |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/test/{pkce,oauth_client}_test.dart` | Leak-as-feature tests flipped to negative regression guards |
| `mobile/lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart` | `load()` discards any persisted verifier containing `.nsec1` and clears storage (defense-in-depth migration) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart` | Error log no longer interpolates `_pendingVerifier` value |
| `mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart` | Removed `authService.exportNsec()` and the `nsec:` arg |
| `mobile/test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart` | **New** — three tests for the migration |
| `mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` | **New** — POSIX-grep guard for production code |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | New `nsec-leak-guard` job |
| `mobile/integration_test/auth/session_expired_banner_test.dart` | `markTestSkipped` until Phase 2 — depends on BYOK preservation |

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test packages/keycast_flutter/{lib,test}` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test packages/keycast_flutter/` — 167/167 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart test/screens/auth/secure_account_screen_test.dart test/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit_test.dart` — 38/38 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/divine_auth/` — 64/64 passing (regression-safety on the path that never carried nsec)
- [x] `bash mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` — exits 0 on this branch
- [x] Guard regex verified: matches `body['nsec']` + `'nsec':`; ignores `containsKey('nsec')` + `any(named: 'nsec')`
- [ ] Manual: e2e secure-account upgrade flow on a local dev stack (post-merge or staging)
- [ ] Coordinate with infra/security on retention review for any pre-fix request bodies that infra-layer components may have captured (separate workstream)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- divinevideo/keycast#197 — server-side proof-of-possession contract (Phase 2A)
- A separate Phase 2 mobile PR — restores BYOK identity preservation via the new server contract (depends on keycast#197 being in production)
- Orphaned ARB key `authUnableToAccessKeys` (no longer referenced from Dart) — left in place to avoid touching 16 locale files; safe to remove in a follow-up

title: ci(ios): add QA PR build slots
body:
Closes #3424

Revives the work from #3440 as a fresh draft PR after reverting the original rollout in #3719.

## Current status

This PR is intentionally back in **draft**. The original merge of #3440 broke Codemagic and had to be reverted. This PR is a straight replay of that original diff onto current `main` so the work can be picked up again deliberately, not merged as-is.

## What broke in the original rollout

Two things made the original rollout unsafe:

1. **`codemagic.yaml` was changed directly**
   - The PR added a new `ios-qa-pr-build` workflow and new QA-slot assumptions around env vars, signing, and distribution.
   - Because `codemagic.yaml` is global CI/CD config, mistakes there can break existing Codemagic behavior immediately, even if app code is fine.

2. **The GitHub allocator workflow tried to trigger Codemagic without guaranteed credentials**
   - The failing run on April 30, 2026 hit a `401` from the Codemagic build trigger.
   - In that run, `CODEMAGIC_APP_ID` and `CODEMAGIC_API_TOKEN` were empty in the workflow environment.
   - The workflow treated that as a hard failure instead of degrading safely, so PR checks went red.

## Root cause

The main problem was not the app identity wiring itself. The problem was that live infra automation was merged before its operational prerequisites were reliably present, and the automation did not fail closed when those prerequisites were missing.

More concretely:
- external setup was still incomplete
- the workflow was active enough to execute anyway
- missing Codemagic credentials produced a hard failure instead of a safe skip/queue state
- too many surfaces were bundled into one PR at once:
  - app identity wiring
  - GitHub Actions allocator
  - Python allocator library/tests
  - Codemagic config
  - docs/specs

## What needs to happen before this can merge again

This PR should be treated as source material for a safer re-rollout, not as merge-ready work.

Recommended rollout plan:

1. **Fail closed when secrets/config are missing**
   - Any automation that triggers external systems must check for required secrets first.
   - If secrets are absent, it should skip or queue, not fail.

2. **Split the rollout into smaller PRs**
   - docs/spec only
   - pure allocator library + tests
   - workflow skeleton that only comments/labels and does not trigger Codemagic
   - Codemagic integration only after secrets and env are confirmed
   - app-side identity wiring only if still needed

3. **Treat `codemagic.yaml` as high-risk infra**
   - Review it separately from normal app code.
   - Require a rollback path before merging.

4. **Gate new automation behind explicit opt-in**
   - Example: require a label like `needs-ios-qa` before allocator/build logic runs.
   - Do not auto-run new infra on every trusted PR on day one.

5. **Add explicit missing-prerequisite handling**
   - missing Codemagic credentials
   - missing Firebase config
   - missing repo variables
   - external API 401/403

6. **Prove the workflow in a throwaway PR before rollout**
   - Validate it with real repo secrets/variables in place.
   - Do not use production PR traffic as the first real test.

7. **Keep external setup separate from active automation**
   - If Chunk 0 setup is incomplete, the workflow should remain inert.
   - Scaffolded but disabled is safer than enabled but half-provisioned.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- This branch currently exists so the original work is preserved and reviewable.
- It should likely be split or partially reimplemented rather than merged intact.
- #3719 reverted the original merge after it broke Codemagic builds.
- #3721 added a temporary guard so the broken allocator workflow would stop hard-failing while the revert landed.

## Summary

This draft PR is here so the iOS QA slot work can be resumed safely. It is **not** a signal that the original rollout shape was sound. The next attempt should be narrower, safer by default, and validated against real secrets/config before merge.

title: feat(nostr): reliable publish primitives + NIP-09 deletion reference migration
body:
Closes #3178

First PR in an 8-PR series to make every Nostr publish in divine-mobile durable. See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-20-reliable-nostr-publish-README.md` for the full plan.

## Summary

- Adds `PublishOutcome`, `NostrClient.publishEventAwaitOk`, `NostrClient.publishEventWithRetry` (bounded exponential backoff, retries only transient relays per NIP-01) — the primitives every follow-up PR uses.
- Adds `PublishResultMapper` so every future service migration maps outcome → user feedback uniformly (success / retryable error / permanent reject with reason).
- Extends `NostrClientStatisticsObserver` with `onPublishOutcome` for per-attempt publish telemetry.
- Migrates `ContentDeletionService` as the reference implementation; `_deleteVideo` in `share_video_menu.dart` now shows a retry-able snackbar on transient failure.
- **Contract change for deletion:** the previous "save locally even if publish fails" branch is removed. Durable deletion now requires at least one relay accept — fixes the ghost-delete bug where the UI believed content was deleted while every other client could still see it.
- Merges cleanly with PR #3117's \`DeleteFailureKind\` localization work — \`DeleteResult\` now carries both \`failureKind\` (pre-publish) and \`outcome\`/\`feedback\` (post-publish).

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/services/content_deletion_service_test.dart` — all 10 existing tests pass against the new `publishEventWithRetry` contract.
- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/unit/services/content_deletion_service_reliability_test.dart` — 3 new tests (success / transient / permanent reject).
- [x] `flutter test mobile/packages/nostr_sdk` — 241+ tests including 7 `PublishOutcome` + 5 `RelayPool.sendAwaitOk` tests.
- [x] `flutter test mobile/packages/nostr_client` — 11 new tests (5 `RetryPolicy` + 6 `PublishResultMapper`).
- [x] `flutter analyze` clean on all changed files.
- [ ] Manually delete a video on a staging relay that drops OK frames — expect retry snackbar with Retry action.
- [ ] Manually delete on a relay that returns \`blocked:\` — expect non-retryable snackbar with the reason.

## Architecture

Four layers, no new top-level packages:

1. **`nostr_sdk/RelayPool`** extends the existing NIP-20 OK handler (previously AUTH-only at `relay_pool.dart:369`) to also resolve pending publishes via per-event completers. New `sendAwaitOk` returns once every target relay has accepted/rejected or the 15s timeout elapses.
2. **`nostr_sdk/Nostr.sendEventAwaitOk`** signs and calls the pool wrapper, returning `PublishOutcome`.
3. **`nostr_client/NostrClient.publishEventAwaitOk`** preserves the existing optimistic-cache + relay-health + cache-rollback behavior. `publishEventWithRetry` wraps it with a `RetryPolicy` (default: 3 attempts, 2s base delay doubled each retry, capped at 30s, 15s per-attempt timeout) and retries only `outcome.transientRelays`.
4. **`nostr_client/PublishResultMapper`** turns a `PublishOutcome` into `PublishUserFeedback{severity, messageKey, retryable, firstRejectionReason}` so UI layers have a single source of truth.

## Out of scope for this PR

The 28 remaining publish call sites (video publish, social graph, DMs, mutes, bookmarks, account deletion, …) migrate in PRs 2–7, and fire-and-forget publishes are annotated in PR 8. Each follow-up plan is in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-20-reliable-nostr-publish-pr*.md`.

title: task(e2e): decide whether to pursue multi-relay persona coverage for Nostr-native users
body:
## Problem

We still do not have strong automated coverage for cross-relay discovery paths that affect Nostr-native users. The current test surface is mostly centered on the Divine / FunnelCake happy path, which leaves room for regressions that only appear when a profile, relay list, and content live across different relays.

## Why This Matters

- Relay discovery via kind `10002` is still a live code path.
- Indexer-based profile discovery is still a live code path.
- Bugs in cross-relay profile/content discovery are exactly the kind that can slip through a single-relay local stack.

## Current Assessment

PR #2508 was a real attempt at this, and the underlying feature idea still makes sense. The strongest value in that draft was the cross-relay persona coverage.

However, that PR is no longer the right merge vehicle. In particular, it introduced local-stack setup debt by baking Android-emulator-specific relay URLs into seeded relay-list data and documenting manual overrides for other platforms. For infrastructure in this repo, the bar is that the local stack should work out of the box rather than requiring platform-specific relay URL patching.

## Decision Needed

Do we still want multi-relay persona coverage in the local stack and E2E suite?

If yes, a fresh follow-up should:
- start from current `main`
- preserve the valuable cross-relay persona coverage goal
- avoid platform-specific manual relay-list overrides as part of normal local-stack use
- keep any notifications coverage narrowly scoped unless it truly exercises the app path it claims to cover

If no, we should close this issue explicitly rather than leave the stale draft PR as background noise.

@dcadenas tagging you here so this gets a clear outcome: if this is still worth pursuing, please drive it forward from a fresh branch/PR against current `main`; if not, please close this issue so we are not carrying it as ambiguous backlog.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide whether multi-relay persona coverage is still desired
- [ ] If yes, re-cut the work from fresh `main` rather than reviving PR #2508
- [ ] Local stack works without platform-specific manual relay URL overrides for the intended supported local test path
- [ ] Cross-relay profile/content discovery is covered by tests that provide real signal
- [ ] Any notifications-related test is described no more broadly than what it actually validates

## Prior Attempt

PR #2508 was the prior draft attempt. It should be treated as historical context only, not as the branch to revive.

title: feat: persistent DB feed cache for instant cold-start loading
body:
## Description

Add a persistent SQLite feed cache to the home and latest feeds, enabling instant video display on cold start via a stale-while-revalidate strategy. Previously, every app launch required a network round-trip before any videos appeared. Now, the last successful feed response is persisted to a Drift `feed_cache` table and served immediately on next launch, while a background revalidation fetches fresh data for the subsequent open.

This replaces the previous `HomeFeedCache` (SharedPreferences) approach which had a stale-data problem: it was written once on initial Funnelcake fetch but never updated by background revalidation, because the DB cache path returned `HomeFeedResult` without `rawResponseBody`. The new approach keeps caching entirely in the repository layer where revalidation can update it directly.

### How it works

**Write path:** When a feed is fetched (from Funnelcake API or Nostr relay fallback), the response is serialized and stored in the `feed_cache` table keyed by feed mode (`"home"`, `"latest"`). Popular mode is excluded (being removed in #2344).

**Read path (cold start):**
1. Check in-memory cache (empty on cold start)
2. Check SQLite DB cache → if found, return cached videos immediately and fire a background revalidation
3. If no cache, fall through to network fetch as before

**Revalidation:** Runs in background (`unawaited`), hits the same Funnelcake API → relay waterfall, and updates both in-memory and DB caches. The BLoC does NOT re-emit after revalidation — fresh data appears on the next user interaction (mode switch, pull-to-refresh, app resume, follow list change). This avoids unexpected UI jank during active scrolling.

### Layers touched

- **Data layer (`db_client`):** New `feed_cache` table with `FeedCacheDao` for CRUD operations. Uses Drift's `DO UPDATE` for upsert semantics.
- **Repository layer (`videos_repository`):** New `_readFeedFromDb` / `_writeFeedToDb` / `_parseCachedFeedBody` helpers. New `_revalidateHomeFeed` / `_revalidateLatestFeed` background methods. Both Funnelcake and relay responses are now persisted (relay goes through `VideoEvent → VideoStats → JSON`).
- **Model layer (`models`):** `VideoStats.toJson()` for serialization. New `VideoStats.fromVideoEvent()` factory so relay-fetched `VideoEvent` objects can be converted to the same `VideoStats` JSON format the cache expects.
- **BLoC layer:** Removed `HomeFeedCache` (SharedPreferences) and its `serveCachedHomeFeed` / `_cacheServed` machinery — superseded by the repository DB cache which is properly updated by revalidation.

### Key design decisions

1. **Stale-while-revalidate over cache-then-network:** The BLoC emits cached data once and does not auto-refresh the UI when revalidation completes. This prevents feed "jumps" mid-scroll but means the user sees data from the previous session until they interact.
2. **Two serialization paths:** Funnelcake responses are stored as raw `response.body` (preserves original format). Relay responses go through `VideoEvent → VideoStats → JSON` since there's no raw body to cache.
3. **Feed key-based storage:** Each feed mode gets its own DB row (`"home"`, `"latest"`). `clearFeedCache()` can clear one or all.
4. **No TTL / max-age on DB cache:** Staleness is handled by always revalidating in background. If the app is killed before revalidation completes, the next open retries.
5. **Removed SharedPreferences cache:** The previous `HomeFeedCache` was never updated after the initial write because the DB cache read path didn't propagate `rawResponseBody`. Rather than fix that plumbing, we consolidated caching in the repository layer where revalidation has direct access.

### What this does NOT change

- The in-memory `InMemoryFeedCache` for instant mode switching is untouched.
- No changes to pagination (only initial page is cached).

## Type of Change

Closes #2313
